prompt:
Image 1 is the target art style. Image 2 is a strip of the scroll 清明上河图 (Along the River During the Qingming Festival) and the only source for what this panel shows. Paint one very wide panel of a painted backdrop in exactly image 1's painting style (hand-inked dark-brown outlines, light hatching, flat muted painted colours, clean readable shapes), showing what image 2 paints, but as a view seen at eye level by a person standing on the ground at the edge of our scene and looking out: looking east out of the town along a country road: the next stretch of the scroll (image 2), seen from its west end at eye level. Image 2's left end is nearest to us and its right end farthest away; its top edge is on our left and its bottom edge on our right. All of it is far off across a stretch of white mist, so even its nearest sheds, animals and people are small, the people's heads on the horizon. The ground lies flat at the horizon as a thin strip; below it there is only white mist. Nearest of all, on the right, one massive old pollard willow with a dark knobbly bole spreads a wide fan of shoots. Then, on the left of the middle: a village stall, a low open-fronted shed under a thatched hip roof with a lower thatched end, a man at its counter and a customer, a water buffalo lying in front of it and an ox standing with its head lowered; behind it a small thatched shed, and three pollard willows standing over the stall. Beside it a small vegetable field in low banked steps, planted with a little grove of young bare trees, thin dark stems with small crab-claw twig crowns, and a wheelbarrow tipped over on the ground. Then a tiled farmhouse with a veranda and a board-walled front wing; on the road before it travellers riding small donkeys, a traveller with a staff, grooms running after a bolting horse. Farther: a low thatched hut behind tall wattle fences, under one huge old willow whose low hollow trunk leans hard over the hut; an open shed on posts; on a track coming down toward us a party returning from the tombs: a tall closed dark sedan chair carried by two bearers, a big spray of long willow twigs fanning up from its roof, a rider on a horse and porters with shoulder poles and boxes. Farthest, on the right: a long low dyke lined with great old pollard willows, massive knobbly boles with roots like rocks, and beyond them a few bare elms. The willows are pollard willows before their leaves open: from each knobbly head a half-open fan of long, straight, stiff bare shoots springs upward and outward. They are NOT weeping willows: no hanging curtains, no drooping strands, no foliage. Early spring: bare branches, no blossom, no green fields. No river, no boats, no bridge, no city, no walls, no towers, no hills or mountains, no lake.

Rules for the panel:
- Only what image 2 paints. Add nothing that image 2 does not show: no hills or mountains, no distant tree lines or forests, no lakes, rivers or islands, no towers, pagodas, city walls, flags, clouds, birds, sun or haze banks, unless the description above names them. Leave out image 2's red seals, inscriptions and silk damage.
- Eye level. The viewer's eye is at the height of a standing person's eyes, so the horizon is one straight, level line across the whole image, a quarter of the way up from the bottom edge. The heads of all standing people are on that line, near or far; buildings, trees, carts and animals rise above it with their feet just under it. Below the horizon there is only a thin strip of level ground, a tenth of the image height at most. We never look down onto roofs, courtyards or the surface of a road: a road running away from us is a thin wedge of ground narrowing to the horizon.
- Plain white everywhere else. The sky is flat pure white from the top edge down to the horizon, behind everything: no clouds, no blue, no gradient, no haze, no texture, no paper grain. Below the strip of ground the bottom of the image is the same pure white: the ground ends in soft white mist. The upper part of the image, above the tallest trees and roofs, is empty white.
- Clear and crisp: every outline and colour as clear as in image 1, with no atmospheric haze and no fading toward the distance (the world adds its own mist). Trees keep clear branches and twigs with white showing between them.
- The left and right eighths of the image hold only low ground and a few small things; they will fade into mist.
- Colours of the real town in soft spring daylight, as in image 1: grey-blue clay tiles, white lime plaster, weathered brown timber, tan rammed earth and dusty roads, pale fresh-green willows, dark green pines, bare ink-brown branches. Not the yellow-brown of the aged silk in image 2; no paper texture, no border, no frame, no seal, no text, no signature.
